title: Maintenance notice cadence and Terraform module guidelines (communications + tagging)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a pragmatic cadence for maintenance notifications for private/VPC/on-prem customers and prescribes small, safe Terraform module conventions to make maintenance windows discoverable and automatable. It is intended as a working draft for solutions engineers, support, and the private deployments team to standardize customer-facing notices and the infrastructure-level metadata we use to power them.

Goals:
- Ensure customers get timely, actionable notices without over-notifying.
- Provide escalation and rollback guidance when an upgrade impacts SLOs.
- Embed machine-readable maintenance metadata into Terraform modules so that automated runbooks and status pages can surface upcoming windows.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineering / Professional Services
- Customer Success & Support
- Platform / Infra on customer-managed deployments
- Product & Legal for SLA alignment

High-level maintenance cadence (recommended)
- Routine patching (non-customer-impacting, e.g., minor agent updates): 14-day notice via email and portal; weekly digest for customers who opt in.
- Planned upgrades (may require short restarts of service): 30-day initial notice, 7-day reminder, 48-hour technical bulletin, 4-hour pre-window confirmation, 30-minute live alert at start.
- Emergency maintenance (security or data integrity issues): Immediate alert + follow-up timeline; formal incident postmortem within 72 hours.

Ownership and RACI (example)
- Product: owns SLA/SLO language and final approval (R).
- Solutions Eng: drafts customer notices and coordinates scheduling (A).
- SRE / Infra: runs the upgrade, provides rollback plan (R).
- Support: sends notices and handles inbound escalation (C).
- Customer: picks preferred maintenance windows and confirms blackout dates (I/C).

Customer-facing templates
(These are short, copy/paste-ready; update placeholders before sending.)

Subject: [Redwood] Planned maintenance for your private deployment – [YYYY-MM-DD] UTC
Body:
Hello [Customer name],

We plan a maintenance window for your private Redwood deployment on [YYYY-MM-DD] from [HH:MM] to [HH:MM] UTC.

What to expect:
- Impact: brief service restart of inference nodes; expected interruption ~[5–15] minutes per replica during the window.
- Reason: rolling runtime upgrade (security patches / performance improvements).
- Mitigation: we will stagger restarts and monitor SLOs; automatic fallback to previous model version if latency degrades beyond thresholds.

If this window conflicts with your blackout dates, reply to this email by [cutoff date]. For technical contact, see your customer success portal or reach out to [SE name] at [se@example.com].

Thanks,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

Subject: [Redwood] Maintenance reminder: 7 days until upgrade (action required?)
Body:
Hello [Customer name],

This is a reminder that the maintenance described in our prior notice is scheduled for [YYYY-MM-DD] at [HH:MM] UTC. If you require a different cadence or have a maintenance freeze, please notify us by [YYYY-MM-DD].

Notes for your ops team:
- No action required unless you have pinned nodes or custom cron jobs that expect continuous connections.
- If you have long-running inference sessions, consider draining connections before the window.

Thanks,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

Emergency alert template
Subject: [Redwood – Action Required] Emergency maintenance for your deployment – immediate
Body:
Hello [Customer name],

We detected a critical issue that affects model correctness/availability for deployments in your region. We will perform an emergency maintenance starting immediately to apply a hotfix. Estimated interruption: [X–Y] minutes.

We will:
- Apply patch and monitor SLOs in real time.
- Escalate to engineering and share a timeline on #private-maintenance at 15-minute cadence.

Contact: oncall-private@[redwood.com]

Post-maintenance: brief summary and next steps will follow within 24 hours.

Operational runbook checklist (ops-facing)
1) Pre-window (72–48 hours):
- Confirm runbook and rollback steps with SRE and SE.
- Populate maintenance metadata in Terraform (see module snippet).
- Run a smoke test in staging with the same config.
- Notify customer (30d/7d flows).

2) Day of (4 hours -> start):
- Verify monitoring (latency, error-rate, token-rate) dashboards are ready.
- Ensure support has templated responses and escalations.
- Quiesce any long-running jobs.
- Begin rolling restarts per plan.

3) Post-window (0–24 hours):
- Confirm SLOs and run targeted quality checks.
- Send a short post-maintenance summary to the customer and close any support tickets.

Terraform module conventions (notes and snippet)
Goal: add simple, standardized metadata fields to the customer-facing TF module so automation can surface upcoming windows in the portal and for on-call scripts. Keep these optional and non-breaking.
Recommended fields to add to module variables:
- var.maintenance_windows (list[string]) – RFC: ISO-8601 windows or human-friendly tags.
- var.maintenance_contact (string) – email or team handle.
- var.maintenance_blackout_dates (list[string]) – customer-specified freeze dates.

Example (pseudo-terraform) – include as comments in module README:

variable "maintenance_windows" {
  description = "Optional list of standard weekly maintenance windows (UTC). e.g. [\"Sun:02:00-04:00\",\"Mon:01:00-02:00\"]"
  type        = list(string)
  default     = []
}

variable "maintenance_contact" {
  description = "Primary contact for maintenance notices (email)."
  type        = string
  default     = ""
}

variable "maintenance_blackout_dates" {
  description = "ISO dates the customer has requested to avoid maintenance."
  type        = list(string)
  default     = []
}

output "maintenance_metadata" {
  description = "Machine-readable map for portal ingestion (json string)."
  value       = jsonencode({ windows = var.maintenance_windows, contact = var.maintenance_contact, blackout = var.maintenance_blackout_dates })
}

Implementation notes:
- Keep defaults empty; do not enforce windows. This avoids surprising upgrades.
- Emit the maintenance_metadata output so the ops automation (portal) can pick it up without changes to state resources.
- Tag provider resources (where applicable) with maintenance:scheduled=true to allow selective queries.

SLO/SLA alignment guidance (customer conversations)
- For Dedicated/private customers we recommend:
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for control plane + 99.9% for data plane (negotiable per contract).
  - Maintenance windows that are announced at least 30 days do not count toward downtime SLA if executed as described in the notice.
- When negotiating, capture: allowed maintenance cadence per quarter, blackout periods, and acceptable max interruption per upgrade.

Rollback decision criteria (examples)
- Latency > 2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes after a rolling update step -> initiate rollback for that shard.
- Error rate spike (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase -> pause rollout and investigate.
- Model quality regression on evaluation suite -> immediate rollback.

Communication channels and observability hooks
- Primary: customer email + portal notice.
- Secondary: status.redwood.ai entry + region-specific Slack channel used for support.
- Observability: dashboard snapshots (pre/post) and perf logs must be attached to the post-maintenance summary.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we provide a webhook from the customer Terraform state to automatically register windows in the portal? (pros: single source; cons: security model).
- Do we allow customers to opt into a monthly maintenance digest vs. discrete notices?
- Determine contract language wording for emergency maintenance that requires immediate action.

Appendix: quick copy for portal tile (short form)
Title: Planned maintenance – [YYYY-MM-DD]
Blurb: Brief restart for runtime upgrade. Estimated interruption: ~10 minutes per replica. Contact: [maintenance_contact].

Notes to self:
- After internal review, push the TF snippet into tf-modules README and add a migration guide for existing customers.
- Coordinate with legal and product for final SLA language before moving to "final" status.

End of draft.
